A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDG-MAE research despite the revised title. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original view-consistency measurements, CDG-MAE training experiments, ablations, and evaluations on DAVIS, VIP, and JHMDB, including additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds optical-flow evaluation, synthetic-data controls, scaling experiments, and generated-view quality and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains offline diffusion-generated views, a shared ViT encoder, masked multi-anchor cross-attention, and pixel reconstruction loss. Additional generators, filtering experiments, and downstream WAFT evaluation test configurations or applications without revising the default CDG-MAE algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates downstream representations only through video label propagation on DAVIS, VIP, and JHMDB. v2 Appendix A.4.5 adds optical-flow estimation, training WAFT on FlyingChairs and FlyingThings and evaluating transfer to KITTI. This substantially extends task and data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 adds evaluated CroCo v1 and v2 baselines, including different model sizes; v1 cited CroCo but did not report these comparisons. Table 10 also adds a CropMAE Real+Synthetic control. These additions broaden comparison to 3D-pretrained methods and directly test a synthetic-data alternative, while retaining the original baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 increases the stated consistency-evaluation sample from 500 to 5,000 images and video-frame pairs. New protocols include two-stage WAFT training with 50K/100K iterations and zero-shot KITTI evaluation, larger-model experiments, and bag sizes of six and eight. The filtering experiment removes 20.4% of training instances while holding training iterations fixed. Original default pretraining and label-propagation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds synthetic-data CropMAE controls, parameter-versus-patch scaling, DINOv2-based consistency checks, classifier-based quality assessment and filtering, and bag-size/masking sensitivity studies. The existing Gen-SIS/RCG analysis is extended with Lumos rather than newly introduced. The comparative pose visualization in v1 Figure 3 is removed, although CDG-MAE-only qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: The original three-seed means and standard deviations, and the single-seed four-anchor results, are retained unchanged in v2 Table 5. Table 15 reuses existing uncertainty estimates and extends the single-seed exploratory reporting practice. No increased repeated-run budget, new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Original headline label-propagation scores are retained, but substantial new results cover CroCo, Lumos, scaling, filtering, robustness, and optical flow. For example, v2 Table 12 reports Stage-2 KITTI endpoint error/F1 of 3.70/11.50 for CDG-MAE versus 3.81/11.75 for CropMAE. Table 14 reports slightly lower scores after filtering. Table 1 consistency values also change under the enlarged sampling protocol, rather than establishing same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The GS, LS, and NPS definitions and the substantive encoder, decoder, and reconstruction equations remain unchanged. Distinguishing mask-token notation in Equation 8 clarifies the existing procedure. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain diffusion-generated views for cross-view MAE, consistency metrics, and multi-anchor masking, with improvements over CropMAE and a narrower gap to video-based methods. v2 emphasizes diffusion-model selection in its headline contribution, but that use was already claimed and demonstrated in v1 Appendix A.4.1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications concerning Lumos pretraining and possible data leakage, the comparability of 3D-pretrained CroCo, and the computational impracticality of video diffusion. New analyses motivate hypotheses about parameter-scaling difficulties and why classifier filtering may sacrifice useful diversity. These extend the original limitation concerning uncontrolled generated variations.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project-code link, specifies the feature space for nearest-neighbor image selection and the 4–48-frame sampling interval, and documents synthetic-image resolution and storage. It also adds detailed optical-flow training settings and expanded resource comparisons. Existing optimizer, hardware, and default training disclosures are retained; the new compute reporting inconsistently labels eight-GPU elapsed hours as GPU hours.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion for Lumos, video-diffusion alternatives, optical-flow pipelines, and classifier-based analysis. It also explains CroCo's distinct 3D-pretraining context. The principal positioning relative to CropMAE, SiamMAE, and self-supervised diffusion remains stable; citation-format changes and duplicate-reference cleanup do not constitute substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related-work prose are substantially revised and tightened. Diffusion-model selection and computational analysis move into dedicated main-text sections, while the appendix is reorganized around expanded supplementary studies. The title and publication presentation also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview diagrams, removes the comparative pose figure, consolidates earlier diffusion-selection and multi-anchor tables, and adds displays for resource comparisons and new analyses. Previously adjacent tables and appendix visualizations are redistributed and resized within a different document layout. Retained plots and examples are distinguishable from genuinely new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support: the synthetic-data CropMAE control addresses a previously untested alternative explanation, optical-flow transfer extends validation beyond label propagation, and backbone, filtering, and scaling studies test important assumptions and limits. Added access and implementation information improves reproducibility. The inconsistent compute units and single-seed exploratory results limit some conclusions, but do not outweigh the substantial gain in controlled and diagnostic evidence.
